paper_id: Zhang et al. - 2015 - Q-Offload Quality Aware WiFi Offloading with Link Dynamics
title: Q-offload: Quality Aware WiFi Offloading with Link Dynamics
motivation: WiFi offloading assumed always energy efficient, but experiments show 45.6% download and 20.1% upload cases consume MORE energy than cellular due to link quality variation
problem_framing: Online knapsack problem with unknown optimal number of knapsacks; NP-hard, no competitive deterministic online algorithm exists
key_insight: Real-time requirements not tight for most traffic; link utilization only 26-30%, allowing rescheduling to good link quality periods
method_signature: Iterative MPC-based framework with dynamic window length, greedy local scheme, and deadline guarantee mechanism
evaluation_criteria: Energy per KB (Eb), throughput, deadline violation ratio; compared with Wiffler, eTime, QATO, Oracle
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Problem NP-hard with no competitive deterministic online algorithm; approximation ratio to oracle is only 0.775 (0.51-0.91); QATO wastes energy in radio state transitions (RRC_PROMOTION, RRC_Tail)
evidence_for_taste: does not admit any competitive deterministic online algorithm
we find that in 45.6% download cases
WiFi offloading brings no energy benefit
approximation ratio between Q-offload and the oracle scheme is not significant
the E_b of QATO is the highest among four schemes
thinking_moves: 从默认假设失效出发：WiFi offloading assumed always energy efficient → empirical falsification
先证计算复杂度下界(NP-hard), 再转向启发式方法(MPC)
把能量优化问题重新frame成link quality scheduling问题
通过CDF量化展示link quality variation的分布特征
区分throughput改善和energy efficiency: QATO throughput相当但Eb最高
